Name: Fluttery Flakes
Author: Spiderbuttons
Description:
This mod replaces the vanilla snow effect with a custom one inspired by the snow effect from SpriteMaster / Clear Glasses. Instead of a consistent wave of identical snowflakes cascading down your screen, this mod will create individual snowflakes that flutter, glide, and float across your screen. This is, to me at least, a more appealing kind of snow effect than vanilla. It removes the vanilla snow completely in favour of the effect from this mod, so if you prefer vanilla, you can skip this mod and stick with it. Or you can try customizing this mod to your liking, since it comes with a range of configuration options available via Generic Mod Config Menu.

If you'd like a preview of what the snowfall looks like on default settings and customized settings, [url=https://github.com/Spiderbuttons/FlutteryFlakes]LOOK HERE[/url].

[b]Installation[/b]
[list]
[*][url=https://smapi.io]Install the latest version of SMAPI[/url].[/*]
[*]Extract the mod into Stardew Valley/Mods.[/*]
[*]Run the game using SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]
[b][size=4]Can I change how the snowfall looks?[/size][/b]
Yes. The snow is pretty highly configurable, so long as you are using Generic Mod Config Menu to do so. You can change things like snow density, wind speed, how fast they rotate, their colour, the background fog, the pixelation, how they move, and the random day-to-day variance of some of these things. The default settings are set to be pretty subtle, so feel free to tune them to your liking. 

[b][size=4]How's the performance?[/size][/b]
The performance cost of this mod will entirely depend on the settings you've configured for it. The default settings, as mentioned, are pretty subtle, and on my machine and 1440p monitor the snowfall has an unnoticeable impact even in full screen with higher than default settings. There are a few key factors that will affect the performance the most:

[list=1]
[*]The snow density. Higher density means more snowflakes, and more snowflakes means more performance cost.[/*]
[*]Screen size. Bigger screens obviously means more snowflakes too, which means more performance cost.[/*]
[*]The frame rate setting. You can choose to have snowflakes be updated at a higher frame rate, which can more or less double the performance cost. I think they look just fine at a lower frame rate, though.[/*]
[*]The snow movement. The "consistent" setting is the cheapest, and the "noisy" setting will incur a higher performance cost the more snowflakes there are on the screen.[/*]
[*]Your zoom level. Again, zoomed out = bigger screen = more snowflakes, you get the idea by now. On the other hand, zooming in means you get [i]better[/i] performance. Vanilla zoom levels should be fine either way, but keep it in mind if you use zoom mods.[/*]
[*]Your mod list. The more stuff you have going on in your game, the more every mod has to share every FPS.[/*]
[*]Split screen. Performance is, honestly, pretty bad in split screen right now. I have plans to make this better in the future.[/*]
[/list]In short: It depends! If you're already struggling to reach 60 FPS, this mod [i]will[/i] make it worse, though at the lowest settings it might still be unnoticeable (and the lowest settings do still look fine). If you can already easily get good frame rates without your computer breaking a sweat, then you will not notice the impact of this mod at all unless you start really cranking up the settings to max.

Inside the configuration screen, you can choose to preview what the snow will look like with your current settings. There is also a "Performance Impact" monitor built into the configuration screen which will show you the estimated number of milliseconds it takes to complete 1 frame, so you can monitor how it changes as you tweak the settings. You need to be able to stay under 16.66 ms/f in order to maintain 60 FPS. Again, it's only an estimate, since different things will happen in your save at different times and such and so the final frame time may fluctuate, but it's still very useful for knowing how your specific settings are affecting things.

[b][size=4]Is this compatible with other weather mods?[/size][/b]
This mod replaces the vanilla snow effect. If other mods implement their own snow effect, then this mod will not replace theirs (and may in fact appear alongside theirs in some cases). If you notice any kind of incompatibility with another mod's snow effect, feel free to let me know and I'll take a look to see if there's anything I can do about it.

[b][size=4]Is this compatible with Clear Glasses' snow?[/size][/b]
No. This is meant to be my own (albeit intentionally inspired by) take on the snow effect from Clear Glasses as its own separate mod. Therefore, the two are not compatible. If you are using Clear Glasses, you should turn off its snow effect if you plan on using mine in order to increase performance. However, the rest of Clear Glasses features will still work on my snow (i.e. my snowflakes will still be smoothed out by its smoothing effect if you have that enabled.)
